title: CIGE 122/2024 Phage characterization
description: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) and multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella has reduced the effectiveness of conventional control measures in poultry production, highlighting the need for alternative strategies such as bacteriophages (BPs). This study aimed to identify the most suitable environmental water sources for isolating lytic BPs against the three major zoonotic Salmonella serovars: Salmonella Enteritidis (SE), Salmonella Typhimurium (ST), and Salmonella Infantis (SI). Twenty-nine field isolates were characterized for antimicrobial susceptibility, and one MDR isolate from each serovar was selected for BP isolation. A total of 128 water samples from eight environmental sources were screened. Overall, 69% of Salmonella isolates showed resistance to at least one antimicrobial, and 50% of resistant isolates were MDR, with SI presenting the highest MDR frequency. Twenty-three lytic BPs were recovered exclusively from urban wastewater, well water, and pig farm wastewater. BPs isolated from urban wastewater and well water exhibited significantly broader lytic spectra than those recovered from pig farm wastewater (P < 0.001). In addition, BPs isolated using SI as the host strain lysed significantly more Salmonella isolates than those obtained using SE or ST. Three urban wastewater-derived BPs (CEU_015, CEU_018, and CEU_022) displayed the broadest host range and were identified as strictly lytic members of the genus Felixounavirus. Genomic analyses confirmed the absence of AMR, virulence, and lysogeny-associated genes. These findings identify urban wastewater and well water as valuable reservoirs of broad-host-range lytic BPs and support the use of Felixounavirus candidates for the development of future biocontrol strategies against Salmonella in poultry production.
